The Story of the Sangasang

In Abra, a sangasang is a traditional spiritual guardian associated with a natural feature, often a tree or large rock. In Barangay Dulao, the community believes its sangasang tree has protected the village for generations. Local stories recount its protection during armed conflict, including an occasion when rebels and government soldiers occupied the same area without ever encountering one another. Beliefs in spirits inhabiting trees, rocks, and other natural features are widespread among Indigenous communities of the Cordillera. These sacred places are treated with deep respect, reflecting a cultural connection between spiritual traditions, nature, and community protection.
